A statistical assistant's processing, review and publication permissions are determined by the position and project; the U.S. occupational classification does not establish a one-to-one correspondence with Chinese positions, qualifications or wages.

The basis for judgment is the U.S. occupational tasks read on this page and the editorial trial design, not a personal diagnosis or hiring standard. An actual position may combine data entry, statistical programming or research support, so look at duties rather than titles.

Suited to people willing to explain clearly how this table was calculated. First complete the data dictionary, the anomaly list and the reproducible summary, observe whether attention holds up under repeated checking, and then decide whether to invest in training.

The work can be organized into three types: data receipt and checking, statistical calculation and tabulation, and file and result maintenance; this is an editorial summary based on official tasks, and an actual position may combine several of them.

O*NET 43-9111.00 gives tasks such as calculating data, checking source materials, maintaining files and preparing charts; its tasks and work context are used for the occupational profile and are not used to infer Chinese qualifications.

entries: Source data checking | Check the completeness, accuracy and field definitions of source records. | Deliver an anomaly list, and do not change unconfirmed problems on your own.
Calculation and summarization | Calculate and tabulate according to confirmed statistical formulas and units. | Deliver reproducible tables and state the denominator, sample and period.
Charts and reports | Compile processing results into charts or reports. | Explain the data scope and limits, and do not write descriptive results as causal conclusions.
File maintenance | Archive data and related notes and maintain databases and files. | Keep the relationship between inputs, dictionaries, programmes and output versions.
Processing programme support | Take part in writing and checking data processing programmes. | Use test records and comparison results to check whether transformations follow the confirmed rules.

Material publication support | Help organize publishable data or information. | Deliver according to project review and permission arrangements, and do not treat a generated file as publication approval.

The following is an editorial five-step processing workflow. Real projects should use methods confirmed by the organization, licensed tools and review arrangements, and this workflow is not written as a uniform regulation.
First confirm field definitions, units, the statistical requirement and processing permission; write clearly who decides the missing value, duplicate and exclusion rules.
Let the tool process only approved materials; require it to produce explicit code and rules and not to fill unknown data by guessing.
Use independent formulas to check the denominator and total, sample and check back on source records, and compare whether the tool changed code, units or missing values.
Keep source files, dictionaries, prompts or programmes, tool versions, run records, anomalies and output versions.
Hand unconfirmed changes and publication matters to the project's designated responsible person; a successful code run cannot substitute for approval.
The tool may supply a plausible-sounding explanation for a wrong variable, which users may misread as a source material conclusion.
Check the data dictionary and source records item by item, and mark explanations that cannot be verified as pending confirmation rather than using them in the published text.
Questionnaires or business records may contain personal information, and uploading, linking and exporting all require checking the processing scope.
Use approved data and tools and minimize inputs; public work uses the simulated materials on this page and not real personal records.
Changes to the model or script will produce different outputs from the same input, and without records they are hard to reproduce.
Seal input and programme versions, keep tool settings and outputs, and compare against a test sample before delivery after changes.
Treating missing values as zero, minutes as hours or duplicate rows as separate will change the mean; attractive charts will not reveal these errors.
First check unique keys, units and the valid denominator, then recalculate totals and statistical tables with independent formulas.

values: Material: simulated service duration table

All are fictional records designed for editing. Each row fields are record number, region, duration and unit: S01 / North / 30 / minutes; S02 / North / 45 / minutes; S02 / North / 45 / minutes; S03 / South / 1 / hour; S04 / South / blank / minutes;
S05 / North / -5 / minutes.

Practice rules: record numbers should be unique; the region may only be North or South; the duration should be non-negative. The original table must be kept and not overwritten directly. You are the processing assistant, and the rule owner has approved: duplicate rows with the same record number and identical four fields keep only one record for the summary; 1 hour is converted to 60 minutes; blanks and negative values are kept in the anomaly table and excluded from the duration mean. Do not fill in values for them.
Task: check and tabulate

Write a four-field dictionary, and check the unique key, region, units, missing values and range; distinguish the original 6 rows, the deduplicated records and the valid-duration records, and list each exclusion with its rule.

Compute the valid record count, total valid minutes and mean by region, and submit the anomaly list and handover notes. This material has no weights, sampling frame or service population information, so do not estimate a population average or satisfaction.
Answer key: recompute independently first

The original 6 rows, with S02 fully duplicated as one row; after deduplication there are 5 unique records. S03 is 1 × 60 = 60 minutes; S04 is blank and S05 = -5 are anomalies in their columns, and the true values are not guessed. The valid-duration records are S01, S02 and S03, 3 in total.

North region has 2 valid records, a total of 30+45=75 minutes and a mean of 75/2 = 37.5 minutes; South region has 1 valid record, a total of 60 minutes and a mean of 60/1 = 60 minutes. The overall total is 135 minutes and the mean is 135/3 = 45 minutes; (37.5+60)/2=48.75 must not be passed off as the overall mean, because the numbers of valid records differ.
Boundary: processing approval and limits on conclusions

Excluding missing and negative values is only because the rules of this exercise explicitly approve it, and does not mean that real projects can exclude them across the board. The South mean describes only 1 valid record; no population, time trend or sampling design is provided, so regional service quality cannot be compared, causality cannot be inferred and real business conclusions cannot be published. Anomalous records and original values are still handed to the rule owner for confirmation.
